title: Dual-Platform Precision Measurement of the $3^2D_{5/2}$ to $4^2S_{1/2}$ $g$-Factor Ratio in $^{40}\text{Ca}^+$
authors: Brian J. McMahon, Vikram S. Sandhu, John M. Gray, Creston D. Herold, Kenton R. Brown, Brian C. Sawyer
abstract: We report precision measurements of the ratio of Landé $g$ factors between the $3^2D_{5/2}$ and $4^2S_{1/2}$ states of a single trapped $^{40}\text{Ca}^+$ ion. The measurements are performed in two distinct ion trap apparatus: a cryogenic surface electrode radiofrequency Paul trap and a room-temperature permanent magnet Penning trap. The Penning trap measurements yield a ratio of $0.599~488~813~3(2)$, which represents a more than 40-fold uncertainty reduction compared to previous work. The radiofrequency trap measurement yields a concurring value of $0.599~488~813(6)$. We estimate that systematic shifts for each system are well below the respective statistical uncertainty.
summary: The authors report highly precise measurements of the $g$-factor ratio for a single $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ion by employing two independent experimental setups: a cryogenic RF Paul trap and a room-temperature Penning trap. By comparing results from these dual platforms, they achieved an unprecedented reduction in measurement uncertainty, providing stringent tests of atomic theory.
main_problem: The primary goal was to achieve a high-precision measurement of the ratio of Landé g-factors between the $3^2D_{5/2}$ and $4^2S_{1/2}$ states in a single trapped $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ion.
main_result: The measurements, performed using two distinct traps (Penning and RF), yielded a highly precise ratio of approximately 0.599488813, reducing the uncertainty by over 40-fold compared to prior work.
method: The experiment employed dual-platform spectroscopy: Rabi/Ramsey measurements in an RF Paul trap and frequency ratios derived from multiple transitions in a Penning trap.
model_or_system: The physical system is a single trapped $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ion. The measurement probes the energy levels of the $S_{1/2}$ and $D_{5/2}$ manifolds, utilizing techniques like Doppler cooling and resolved-sideband cooling.
important_parameters: Penning trap field ($\sim 0.91 	ext{ T}$ axial); RF trap field ($0.7 	ext{ mT}$).
main_assumptions: Systematic shifts from various sources (e.g., AC Stark, linear Zeeman drift) were estimated to be smaller than the statistical uncertainty in both measurement platforms.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the spectroscopy techniques used in both the Penning and RF traps. Figure 2 shows repeated measurements confirming the final reported value for the g-factor ratio using the Penning trap setup.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental methodology, comparing results from two complementary trapping environments (Penning vs. RF). It presents the derived ratio values, analyzes systematic error mitigation techniques specific to each trap, and concludes by stating the combined high-precision result.
why_interesting: This work represents a state-of-the-art example of precision measurement in trapped ions, directly testing fundamental atomic structure constants ($g$-factors) using complementary quantum interrogation methods. The comparison between two vastly different physical platforms (RF vs. Penning) is particularly valuable for validating results.
